key_idea: Run Dijkstra from s and from t on the undirected road graph; a path using flight (u,v) costs ds[u] + dt[v], so take the minimum over all flights and the no-flight distance.
sketch: Roads are undirected, so one Dijkstra from s and one from t give all needed distances. Answer = min(ds[t], min over flights u->v of ds[u] + dt[v]). O((n+m) log n + f). Pitfalls: flights are directed, so only ds[u]+dt[v] and not the reverse; use 64-bit distances (up to about 2.5e9) with a large but non-overflowing infinity since unreachable endpoints get added together; m can be 0.
